docs.title: corpus
docs.text:
corpus renders a styled corpus figure from a tidy CSV you already have, as plot_corpus_figure does. For --kind profile the CSV needs word_id and value columns.

scanpath-studio corpus --input profile.csv --kind profile --output profile.svg
Option Value Default Description --input PATH required The CSV. profile reads word_id and the value column, plus optional lo and hi; distribution reads the value column; difference reads word_id and diff. --kind profile, distribution, difference required A per-word profile, a distribution, or a difference profile. -o--output PATH required Output file; any extension save_figure writes (.html, .png, .svg, .pdf). --measure-label MEASURE_LABEL Value Axis and legend label for the value (default: Value). --series-col SERIES_COL series Column naming the overlaid series, when present (default: series). --value-col VALUE_COL value The value column (default: value). --primary-color PRIMARY_COLOR #1f77b4 First series color (default: #1f77b4). --secondary-color SECONDARY_COLOR #e45756 Second series color (default: #e45756).

docs.title: check
docs.text:
check runs the Data Management page's Data checks on your tables without opening the app. It looks for:

  • fixations lasting 0 ms or less, or with an infinite duration or onset;
  • fixations and raw gaze samples with no finite position, or one more than a million pixels off the screen;
  • word boxes with no area, or no finite position or size within a million pixels;
  • screen sizes that are not finite and positive.

Each finding gives the rows and trials affected, a few example rows, and what the app does with them. check changes nothing and exits 0 whatever it finds. --json prints the table check_data_health returns.

scanpath-studio check --words ia.csv --fixations fixations.csv
scanpath-studio check --raw-gaze gaze_samples.csv --json
Option Value Default Description --sample switch — Check the bundled demo instead of your own tables. --words PATH [PATH ...] — Words table(s), as for render. --fixations PATH [PATH ...] — Fixations table(s), as for render. --raw-gaze PATH [PATH ...] — The Raw gaze table, as for render. --raw-gaze-schema JSON — Column mapping for the --raw-gaze table, replacing auto-detection, in the form --fix-schema takes. --trial-parts-manifest PATH — JSON manifest assigning source rows to ordered screens. --json switch — Print the findings as JSON (the rows api.check_data_health returns). --word-schema JSON — Column mapping for the --words table, replacing auto-detection. A JSON object from each field to a column name, or the path of a JSON file holding one, e.g. '{"trial": "TRIAL_INDEX", "word_id": "IA_ID", ...}'. It is the dict api.load_scanpath_data takes. Needed only when a column isn't recognized, and the error then prints a mapping to start from. --fix-schema JSON — Column mapping for the --fixations table, replacing auto-detection. A JSON object from each field to a column name, or the path of a JSON file holding one, e.g. '{"trial": "TRIAL_INDEX", "word_id": "IA_ID", ...}'. It is the dict api.load_scanpath_data takes. Needed only when a column isn't recognized, and the error then prints a mapping to start from. --keep-columns COLUMN [COLUMN ...] — More columns to keep through loading, under the names they have in your files (e.g. a pupil size), from whichever table has them. Without it, loading keeps only the mapped and recognized fields. A kept fixation column can be used by --color-by, an axis or a hover. Same as keep_columns= in api.load_scanpath_data.

docs.title: cache
docs.text:
A local or desktop run saves your session on your computer, so a refresh or a restart resumes where you left off. It saves uploaded datasets, column mappings, view settings, saved designs, metadata tables and annotations. cache shows what is stored and can delete it.

scanpath-studio cache            # datasets, rows, size, folder, last written
scanpath-studio cache --path     # just the folder
scanpath-studio cache --json     # the same status as JSON
scanpath-studio cache --clear    # delete the recovery cache
Option Value Default Description --path switch — Print the cache folder and exit. --json switch — Print the status as JSON. --clear switch — Delete the recovery cache.

The same information is at the foot of the Data Management page, under Saved on this computer. A running app writes a new copy at its next change, so clear the cache with the app closed.

To Use turn caching off for one launch scanpath-studio --no-persist turn it off wherever the variable is set SCANPATH_STUDIO_PERSIST=0 move the folder SCANPATH_STUDIO_STATE_DIR

Hosted deployments do not cache by default.

docs.title: version
docs.text:
version says which build this is and how it was installed. --check also asks GitHub whether a newer release is out and says how to update your install. Only --check uses the network.

scanpath-studio version           # the build, and how it was installed
scanpath-studio version --check   # …and whether a newer release is out
Option Value Default Description --check switch — Ask GitHub for the latest release and say how to update this install. --timeout SECONDS 5.0 How long to wait for GitHub, in seconds (default: 5).

Between releases the version names the build: 0.35.0.post3+g8f18219 is three commits after 0.35.0, at commit 8f18219. The same check is Help → About → Check for updates in the app, and check_for_updates in Python.

docs.title: cite
docs.text:
cite prints how to cite Scanpath Studio. --corpus adds the citation of the public corpus you used.

scanpath-studio cite                           # BibTeX
scanpath-studio cite --format apa --corpus onestop
scanpath-studio cite --format credit           # one sentence for a figure caption
Option Value Default Description --format bibtex, apa, ris, csl-json, credit bibtex Bibtex (default), apa, ris (Zotero, Mendeley, EndNote), csl-json, or credit: one sentence to paste into a figure caption. --corpus onestop, potec — Add this public corpus's citation after the software's.

You don't have to add the citation to your files by hand: every figure render writes carries it in its file metadata. The same entries are cite in Python.

docs.title: The fixations don't line up with the text
docs.text:
Words and fixations must use the same pixel coordinates and share trial IDs. If the fixations are shifted, mirrored or scaled against the words, the two tables use different coordinates: a different origin, unit or offset. No setting in the app fixes that, so convert one of the tables (What your data needs → Files and units).

If the fixations sit on the words but the figure is framed or sized wrongly, set the screen resolution of the monitor used in the experiment. Open Data Management → Edit dataset → Recording setup and choose Screen → I know it. Estimate from my data gives only a lower bound.

docs.title: The text is too big or too small
docs.text: The text is drawn to scale from the word boxes and the recording screen size. Set the real resolution first (see above). For OneStop it is 2560×1440, and in Python you pass canvas_size=(2560, 1440). If the text is still off, set the line spacing under Recording setup → Text size → Fit to word boxes, or line_spacing= in Python. Line spacing is the distance between lines, in font sizes.

docs.title: A column was detected wrongly
docs.text: The app guesses columns from their names. Pick the right one under Data Management → Edit dataset, or pass word_schema / fix_schema to load_scanpath_data.

docs.title: Can I load only one table?
docs.text: Yes. A Words table alone shows the text and any reading measures it carries. A Fixations table alone shows the fixations without the text. A Raw gaze table can also be the only table. Most features need both words and fixations. When your tables cover different trials, every trial that any of them has is listed and drawn with the layers it has.

docs.title: Can I open PoTeC or OneStop in the online demo?
docs.text: No. The online demo has only the bundled demo, and it doesn't download public datasets. In the desktop app or a pip install, each public dataset downloads once, with one click, and stays on your computer.

docs.title: My zip file is refused as too large
docs.text: The app limits how far a .zip may decompress: 32 GB per file and 64 GB in total. The error names the setting that raises the limit, for example SCANPATH_ZIP_MAX_MEMBER_GB=64 scanpath-studio.

docs.title: Does the app compute reading measures?
docs.text: No. Corpus Analysis and Export show the reading measures in your Words table, as your eye-tracking software defines them (Reading measures).

docs.title: Does  Filters & highlights change my data?
docs.text: No. It changes only what the figure draws. Your tables and measures stay as they are.

docs.title: Image or video export fails
docs.text: These exports need Chrome, Chromium or Edge on the computer that runs Scanpath Studio: PDF, GIF and MP4 files, static images from Python or the CLI, and export bundles with images. Installing one of these browsers is enough. With a pip install you can instead run plotly_get_chrome -y once. HTML files, and the current figure's PNG and SVG, work without a browser.

docs.title: Can someone else open my share link?
docs.text: Yes, but the link does not contain your data, so they need to load the same dataset first. The bundled demo opens directly. A public dataset opens if they have it set up.

docs.title: Where does my data go?
docs.text: When you run Scanpath Studio locally or as the desktop app, your data stays on your computer. There are no accounts, and scanpath-studio and the desktop app send no usage statistics. The online demo runs on Streamlit Community Cloud, whose page around the app has its own analytics (privacy policy). See Your data for what a local install saves, where, and how to clear it.

docs.title: Can I share a figure without showing the text?
docs.text: Yes. Turn on Stimulus ▾ → Text → Redact. Each word becomes a rounded block over its letters, so the figure keeps the layout of the text but none of its words. Hovers and saved HTML hide the words too. Also turn off the stimulus image, since it shows the screen as it was. On the command line, use render --redact-text, and in Python redact_text=True. The data tables and exported tables still hold the words.

docs.title: Will a refresh lose my work?
docs.text:
Not on a local or desktop install. When the app listens only on this computer, as scanpath-studio and the desktop app do, it saves your datasets and settings there. Data Management → Saved on this computer shows what it holds. The online demo keeps nothing and says so after your first upload, so export your annotations and settings before you leave (what to back up).

If the files of one saved dataset go missing or are damaged, the rest of the session still comes back. The app names the dataset it could not restore, keeps that saved copy unchanged, and offers Retry and Remove saved copy. Saved metadata tables that can't be read are kept the same way. If the whole saved copy can't be read, the app opens without it and stops saving over it until you retry or clear it.

docs.title: How do I stop saving, or delete what is saved?
docs.text: Start the app with scanpath-studio run --no-persist to save nothing. To delete what is saved and start over, use Clear what is saved… under Saved on this computer, or close the app and run scanpath-studio cache --clear. That leaves the public datasets you downloaded: delete one with its button in the same section. See Your data and Recovery cache.

docs.title: Where do I ask a question, report a bug or send feedback?
docs.text:
Help → Send feedback links each kind of feedback to its page on GitHub: Report a bug, Suggest a feature, Share an idea and Ask a question. It also shows the version and system details a bug report needs, ready to copy. The app sends nothing. You submit each one on GitHub yourself.

Ask questions in Discussions → Q&A. Report a bug as a GitHub issue, with the version, your operating system and how you run the app (pip, the desktop app or the online demo). Help → About shows the version and links to both. On the command line, run scanpath-studio --version.

docs.title: How do I update Scanpath Studio?
docs.text:
Open Help → About → Check for updates. In the desktop app, choose Update & restart. For a Python install, run:

pip install -U scanpath-studio

docs.title: Will my links, settings and scripts work after an update?
docs.text: Not necessarily. Until version 1.0, any release may change the app, its share links and saved settings, the Python API and the CLI. The changelog lists the changes in each release. To reproduce a result, note the version you used and install that one: pip install scanpath-studio==<version>.

docs.title: How do I cite Scanpath Studio?
docs.text: See Cite Scanpath Studio for BibTeX and APA entries, and Bundled demo for the bundled demo's source. In the app, Cite under each download gives the same entries, and every exported file carries the citation in its metadata (Cite what you export).

docs.title: Across the experiment
docs.text:
Mean total fixation duration per word across one participant’s trials in the bundled demo. Each point is one trial. The bundled demo holds only part of the session.

In the appCLIPython
  1. Open your data in the Corpus Analysis view, on the Per participant tab.
  2. Choose a participant, and in View choose Per-trial trend.
  3. Choose a reading measure your data provides, and Mean in Aggregate. The horizontal axis is the trial order from the data’s trial_index or TRIAL_INDEX column. Without one, the app orders the trials by fixation time, or as listed.

Follow the progression tutorial

The corpus CLI does not offer trial-order trends. Download the Python recipe and run:

python across-experiment.py

This uses the app’s aggregation and trend builder.

import scanpath_studio as sps

from scanpath_studio.aggregation import metric_by_trial_index
from scanpath_studio.data import derive_trial_index
from scanpath_studio.plots import make_trend_figure

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data(names="canonical")
reader = words[words["participant_id"] == "l37_1129"].copy()
reader["trial_index"] = derive_trial_index(reader)
trend = metric_by_trial_index(reader, "total_fixation_duration_ms")
fig = make_trend_figure(
    trend,
    x_col="trial_index",
    x_label="Recorded trial order",
    y_label="Mean total fixation duration per word (ms)",
    title="Across the experiment · Participant A",
    canvas_width=1000,
    base_font_size=18,
    font_family="Arial",
    height=450,
    break_gaps=True,
)

sps.save_figure(fig, "across-experiment.html")

docs.title: Fully customizable
docs.text:
Make a figure for a talk or teaching: pink hearts for fixations, purple arrows for the eye’s movements. This hand-drawn illustration follows The → cat → sat → on → the → mat, with one fixation per word.

In the appCLIPython
  1. Load your Words and Fixations tables, or the example words and fixations. For the example, set Recording setup → Screen to I know it, 450 × 300 px. Open the dataset in the Scanpath view and pick a trial in Select trial.
  2. In Fixations ▾ → Marker, set Shape to ♥ Heart. Keep Color at One color and set its box to #d12d72. Set Size to 18–30 and Opacity to 0.85. Tick Snap → To line, and leave Fixation index → Show unticked.
  3. In Saccades ▾, set Shape to Arc. Under Line, keep Color at One color with #4f46a5, and set Width to 2.5. Tick Direction arrows and set Arrow size to 12.
  4. In Figure & canvas ▾ → Legends, untick Show for Fixation sizes. Under Title & labels → Illustration, enter “Illustration · hand-drawn” in Text. Leave Stimulus ▾ → Highlight words unticked.

Save the look under My designs to apply it to your own data.

Open the demo · All controls

Download the example words and fixations into the same folder.

scanpath-studio render --words words.csv --fixations fixations.csv \
  -p synthetic -t synthetic_2line_demo --canvas 450x300 \
  --fixation-symbol heart --fixation-color '#d12d72' \
  --marker-size-range 18 30 --fixation-opacity 0.85 --snap-fixations \
  --saccade-arcs --saccade-arrows --saccade-color '#4f46a5' \
  --saccade-width 2.5 --saccade-arrow-size 12 \
  --no-fixation-index --no-duration-size-legend --highlight-column '' \
  --illustration-text "Illustration · hand-drawn" -o hearts-arrows.html

import scanpath_studio as sps

from scanpath_studio.synthetic import make_synthetic_words

words = make_synthetic_words()
fixations = words[["participant_id", "trial_id", "text_id", "word_id"]].copy()
fixations["x"] = words["x"] + words["width"] / 2
fixations["y"] = words["y"] + words["height"] / 2
fixations["duration_ms"] = [100, 150, 120, 200, 90, 110]
fixations["timestamp_ms"] = (
    fixations["duration_ms"].cumsum() - fixations["duration_ms"]
)
fixations["order_in_trial"] = range(1, len(fixations) + 1)
fixations["pass_index"] = 1
pid, tid = "synthetic", "synthetic_2line_demo"
fig = sps.plot_scanpath(
    words,
    fixations,
    pid,
    tid,
    canvas_size=(450, 300),
    fixation_symbol="heart",
    fixation_color="#d12d72",
    marker_size_range=(18, 30),
    fixation_opacity=0.85,
    fixation_snap_to_line=True,
    saccade_render_mode="Arc",
    show_saccade_arrows=True,
    saccade_color="#4f46a5",
    saccade_width=2.5,
    saccade_arrow_size=12,
    show_order=False,
    duration_size_legend=False,
    illustration_text="Illustration · hand-drawn",
)

sps.save_figure(fig, "hearts-arrows.html")

docs.text:
Open a tab, then pick a figure in its View menu.

Tab Use it to Per text Compare word-by-word reading across participants Per participant Inspect one participant across trials Groups Describe a group of trials, or compare two, such as two conditions

Choose the Measure, how to Aggregate it and, where a view draws a band, its Spread. For word profiles, set Min participants per word.

docs.title: Supply reading measures
docs.text: Word-level views use the reading measures in your data, such as first fixation duration or total fixation duration. Map those columns when you import. Views of single fixations, such as Fixation duration over time, use the Fixations table.

docs.title: Compare groups
docs.text: Under Define groups by, choose Split a field to pick a group by the values of one field, or Independent filter sets to build it from filters. Turn on Compare a second group to define a group B and see the two groups side by side, their means and their difference. These views are descriptive and run no significance tests.

docs.title: Save results
docs.text: Under each result, ⬇ Download this table (CSV) saves the table and ⬇ Download the recipe (JSON) saves how it was made: the dataset, the trial filters, the analysis choices and the counts. The recipe holds no data rows and no figure settings. To inspect single trials, return to the Scanpath view.

docs.title: Plot a summary in code
docs.text:
Start from a tidy summary table, such as a Cohort profile table downloaded from Corpus Analysis. A word profile needs word_id and value columns, with optional lo and hi for a band. The downloaded table names the word ID column as your data does, so rename it to word_id if needed. For a trend over trial order, see Across the experiment.

Python and CLI: word profile PythonCLI 
import pandas as pd
import scanpath_studio as sps

profile = pd.read_csv("profile.csv")
fig = sps.plot_corpus_figure(
    profile, kind="profile", measure_label="Total fixation duration (ms)"
)
sps.save_figure(fig, "profile.html")

scanpath-studio corpus --input profile.csv --kind profile \
  --measure-label "Total fixation duration (ms)" -o profile.html

API parameters · CLI options

docs.title: Export and share
docs.text: Save a figure, export many trials at once, or reuse a view in the app or in code.

docs.title: In the app
docs.text:
Goal Where Save the figure or replay on screen Export → Current figure Export many trials and their tables Export → Export bundle Share a view or copy its code Share → Link or Code Reuse the figure settings My designs, or Share → Settings file

In Essentials mode, Export holds Current figure only; Export bundle is in Full.

For step-by-step instructions, see the export tutorials.

docs.title: Cite what you export
docs.text:
Every file you export says how to cite Scanpath Studio in its own metadata: the PNG's text chunks, the SVG's <metadata>, the PDF's document properties, the HTML page's <head>, and the GIF's and MP4's comment. Nothing is drawn on the figure.

  • Cite, under each download and in Share → Code, gives a one-line figure credit, the APA reference and BibTeX, and .bib and .ris files for Zotero, Mendeley or EndNote. For the bundled demo, OneStop or PoTeC, it cites the corpus too.
  • An export bundle has a CITATION.bib, and its README.md a Cite section.
  • Figure & canvas → Credit adds a small Made with Scanpath Studio line under the plot, for a figure shared without its caption. In code, pass show_credit=True, or --credit to render.
  • In code, cite and scanpath-studio cite print the citation.

A link reopens the trial and its settings for anyone who has the same dataset. All controls → Under the plot says what the recipient needs.

docs.title: Reproduce a figure
docs.text:
Open Share → Code and copy the Python or CLI code. It carries the figure's settings and your column mapping. For a dataset you imported, replace the placeholder file paths with your own. Render in code shows a minimal example.

For a PNG at print size, pass width_mm and dpi to save_figure, or --width-mm and --dpi to render. To edit the layers in a vector editor, save each layer to a separate file with save_figure_layers or render --separable-layers. In the app's export bundle, this is Layers as separate files.

docs.title: Batch export
docs.text:
In the app, Export bundle → Trials to include picks the trials: This trial, All filtered trials, All trials of one participant, All trials of one text or All trials, ignoring filters. For a scripted batch, loop over the trial list:

Python: one HTML figure per trial 
from pathlib import Path

import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
out = Path("figures")
out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

for pid, tid in sps.list_trials(words, fixations).itertuples(index=False):
    fig = sps.plot_scanpath(words, fixations, pid, tid)
    sps.save_figure(fig, out / f"{pid}_{tid}.html")

Use the data loaders for your own files. The CLI's render writes one trial per run.

docs.title: Replay export
docs.text:
With Animate on, Export → Current figure saves the replay as HTML, GIF or MP4. The CLI's render --animate saves interactive HTML only. For a GIF or MP4 in Python:

Python: save a GIF or MP4 
from pathlib import Path

import scanpath_studio as sps
from scanpath_studio.animation_export import export_animation

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
replay = sps.animate_scanpath(words, fixations, "l37_1129", "l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele")
Path("replay.mp4").write_bytes(export_animation(replay, fmt="mp4"))

Use fmt="gif" and a .gif filename for GIF output.

docs.title: Data Management
docs.text: Load your own data, open a public dataset, or try the bundled demo.

docs.title: Choose a dataset
docs.text:
Pick a dataset in Select dataset above the plot, or in the dataset list on the Data Management page:

  • Bundled demo: 24 trials from OneStop, with two participants and 12 texts.
  • Hand-drawn sample: a scanpath drawn by hand over a short English text, which you can edit.
  • Public datasets: OneStop and PoTeC. In the desktop app or a pip install, each downloads the first time you open it.
  • + → Import files: your own tables.
  • + → Draw a scanpath: write a text and place its fixations by hand.

docs.title: OneStop
docs.text: The bundled demo comes from OneStop Eye Movements (Berzak et al., 2025), an English corpus with 360 participants. The full corpus is available as four public datasets: OneStop · Ordinary reading, OneStop · Information seeking, OneStop · Repeated reading and OneStop · Information seeking (repeated). Each downloads once from OSF.

docs.title: What your data needs
docs.text:
A dataset needs at least one of the first three tables below. Add the others as you need them.

Table Contents Fixations One row per fixation: trial ID, duration, and x/y or a word ID Words (interest areas) One row per word: trial ID, word ID and word box Raw gaze One row per gaze sample: trial ID, x and y Participants One row per participant, with metadata Trials One row per trial, with metadata Texts One row per text, with metadata

The app detects columns from common eye-tracker exports. Check and correct the mapping when you import. To keep condition labels and other columns, pick them under Extra fields to keep. You can filter, sort and group trials by any metadata field.

docs.title: Files and units
docs.text:
• CSV, TSV, TXT, Parquet, Feather, Excel, or a ZIP of these files
  • Positions in pixels
  • Times in milliseconds. A time column whose header names its unit, such as [s], [μs] or [ns], is converted.
  • Word boxes as x/y/width/height or EyeLink's IA_LEFT/RIGHT/TOP/BOTTOM
  • Word IDs as numbers, or as text such as w1. Spell text IDs the same way in the Fixations and Words tables. With text IDs, the order of the rows in the Words table sets the word order.

docs.title: Trials over several screens
docs.text: Map the Screen ID field in your tables. A column named screen_index sets the order of the screens. Without one, the screens are ordered by where they first appear. The app draws one screen at a time.

docs.title: Reading measures
docs.text: Corpus Analysis uses the per-word reading measures in your Words table, such as first fixation duration or total fixation duration. Map them when you import. EyeLink's IA_* columns are detected.

docs.title: Add your own data
docs.text:
1. Choose + → Import files and name the dataset.
  2. Upload your tables and check the column mapping.
  3. Under Recording setup, enter the Screen, Monitor width and Text size if you know them.
  4. Optionally, in the desktop app or a local install, attach the stimulus images from a folder.
  5. Click Add dataset, then Open in Scanpath to see its first trial. Later, Open in Scanpath beside Add dataset on the Data page does the same for the selected dataset.

docs.title: Load and inspect in code
docs.text:
Load the same files in a script. The loaders detect column names the same way the app does.

Python and CLI PythonCLI 
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_scanpath_data("ia.csv", "fixations.csv")
print(sps.list_trials(words, fixations))

scanpath-studio render --words ia.csv --fixations fixations.csv --list-trials
scanpath-studio check --words ia.csv --fixations fixations.csv

For raw gaze, metadata and explicit column mappings, see the loaders and CLI input options.

docs.title: Manage datasets
docs.text:
Click a dataset in the dataset list to open it. Below the list, What's in ‹dataset› shows its tables, annotations and Data checks. When a check flags more than half of a table, such as every duration read as 0 ms, the Scanpath view says so above the plot.

Use Edit dataset to change its name, column mapping, recording setup or metadata, then click Save changes. Download setup file saves the mapping and recording setup, so you can apply them to similar data.

The editor offers only the columns kept when the dataset was added. To use a column that isn't listed, remove the dataset and add it again from its files, mapping the column or keeping it under Extra fields to keep.

docs.title: Scanpath visualization
docs.text:
1. Views and Help.
  2. The trial control bar: dataset, trial, screen, sort (⇅) and filter ().
  3. The trial's summary.
  4. The figure.
  5. Plot controls.
  6. The tabs: Annotations, Stimulus & context, Comparisons, Export and Share.

The Scanpath view draws one reading at a time, at the size of the screen it was recorded on.

Looking for a specific button?

All controls lists every button and setting on this view, menu by menu, with a picture of each menu. Search it for what you want to change, such as saccade color or legend position.

docs.title: Essentials and Full
docs.text:
The view opens in Essentials, a trimmed version of the same view for a first look. The Essentials | Full switch is in the top bar, on the Scanpath view only. The mode you choose is remembered in this browser. Adding ui=full (or ui=essentials) to the app's address, as ?ui=full or &ui=full, uses that mode for the visit without changing the saved choice, and a link made with Share does not carry the mode.

Essentials shows:

  • the dataset and trial pickers with ◀ ▶;
  • the plot, which on a new visit opens on a playing replay;
  • four view tiles (Animation, Scanpath, Heatmap and Illustration) and the Palette;
  • the Export tab, for the figure on screen, and Share.

Where Full has more, a More button lists what it adds there and ends in Switch to Full. A setting made in Full, such as a trial filter, still shapes the figure in Essentials, and Essentials says so in a short note. Starting a tutorial from Help switches that visit to Full. Corpus Analysis and Data Management are the same in both modes.

The numbered regions above and the rest of this guide describe Full.

docs.title: Choose a trial
docs.text:
Pick a trial in Select trial above the plot, or step through the list with ◀ ▶. The filter () beside it narrows the list by text, participant, condition or annotation, and ⇅ sorts it. On a trial recorded over several screens, Screen picks the screen to draw. When several participants have the same trial ID, the list shows each reading with its participant in brackets, such as 3 [p2].

All controls → Trial control bar describes each control.

docs.title: Control the layers
docs.text:
The Plot controls column, on the right of the plot, holds the figure's settings. Each layer has a row with a switch that turns it on or off and a ▾ that opens its settings.

Section What it controls Animate replay the fixations in the order they happened, at a speed you choose Compare draw a second reading over this one, beside it or below it Design presets restyle the whole figure in one click: Scanpath, Heatmap, Illustration, or Custom for your most recent settings My designs save the current settings as a design, apply it again in one click, or export your designs to share them or use them on another computer Palette one color scheme for the whole figure: Default (colorblind-safe), Print / grayscale or High contrast Fixations the fixation markers: color, shape and size, and the fixation index Saccades the saccade lines and arrows, in one color, by direction or by saccade type Stimulus the text (or redacted blocks), highlighted words, the stimulus image, the font and the background Word boxes each word's box: outline and fill, color and opacity Heatmap where fixations concentrate, by fixation count or duration Raw gaze the gaze samples as recorded Filters & highlights which fixations and saccades are drawn, and which stand out Figure & canvas screen framing, axes and grid, title and labels, hover fields and legends

All controls → Plot controls describes every setting in each menu.

docs.title: Under the plot
docs.text:
Tab What it is for Annotations Star, tag and write notes on the trial, to find or filter it later. Stimulus & context The trial's context, such as its title, question and answers, and its highlighted word spans. Comparisons Show the other trials that share a field with this one, such as other readings of the same text, in a grid of small figures. Export Download the figure on screen (PNG, SVG, PDF or HTML) or its replay (HTML, GIF or MP4), or build a zip bundle of figures and data for many trials. Share Link reopens this trial with these settings for anyone who has the same dataset. Code gives the Python or CLI code that redraws the figure. Settings file saves the plot settings and restores them.

All controls → Under the plot lists each tab's controls.

Watch the tabs under the figure

docs.title: Render in code
docs.text:
Set up a figure in the app, then open Share → Code for the Python or CLI code that redraws it. For a dataset you imported, replace the placeholder file paths with your own.

Python and CLI: render the demo PythonCLI 
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
fig = sps.plot_scanpath(words, fixations, "l37_1129", "l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele")
sps.save_figure(fig, "scanpath.html")

scanpath-studio render --sample \
  -p l37_1129 -t l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele -o scanpath.html

For your own files, use the data loaders. The figure options table lists every figure setting with its Python keyword and CLI flag. For more CLI examples, see Common tasks.

The gallery shows how to make heatmaps, comparisons, replays and other figures in the app, the CLI and Python. For batch export and GIF or MP4 replays, see Export and share.

docs.title: Back up your work
docs.text:
You can save each of these to a file and load it again:

What Where figure settings Share → Settings file favorites, tags and notes Data Management → Annotations → Export column mapping and recording setup Edit dataset → Download setup file saved figure designs My designs → Export

None of these files holds your data, so load the same data before you restore one. In the desktop app or a local install, the app also keeps your datasets, annotations and designs between sessions. See Data Management → Saved on this computer.

docs.title: All controls
docs.text:
Every control in the Scanpath view, where it is and what it does, in the order you meet them on screen. Search this page (Ctrl+F, or Cmd+F on a Mac) for the thing you want to change, such as colors, legends or axes.

The view has two sets of controls:

  • The trial control bar, above the plot, decides what you see: the dataset, the trial, and which trials are in the list.
  • The plot controls, the column on the right, decide how it is drawn: each layer of the figure, its colors and sizes, and the figure as a whole.

The tabs under the plot then work with the trial on screen: annotate it, read its context, compare it, export it or share it. For how the parts fit together, see the Scanpath visualization guide.

For the corresponding Python keywords and CLI flags, use the figure options table.

docs.title: Trial control bar
docs.text:
The bar above the plot: pick a dataset and a trial, step through the trials, and narrow, sort or label the list. Essentials has all of it except the slider, ⇅, the filter () and the trial summary table with its pencil (), which are in Full.

Control What it does Select dataset The dataset the view shows. → Draw a scanpath Write a text and place its fixations by hand, as a new dataset. → Import files Upload your own Fixations and Words tables as a new dataset. Select trial The trial to show. Click it and type to narrow the list. Slider Move through the trials in the list. ◀ ▶ The previous or next trial. ⇅ → Sort trials by Reorder the trial list by a statistic (such as reading time), a participant, text or condition field, or a column of a metadata table you attached. ⇅ → Descending Reverse that order. → Text / Participant Keep only these texts or participants. Empty keeps all. → a field of your data Keep only trials with these values, or, for a number, in this range. → By participant / By trial / By text The same, for the columns of an attached metadata table. → Favorites only Keep only starred trials. → With any of these tags Keep only trials with any of these tags. → Excluding tags Hide trials with any of these tags, such as To exclude. → ✕ Clear all filters Reset every filter in the panel. → Show the trial summary above the plot Show or hide the row of facts about the trial above the plot. → field lists Drag fields between Shown and Available to choose the trial summary's fields, and drag within Shown to reorder them. Available holds every field with one value per trial: participant, text and condition columns, the columns of any metadata table you attached, and statistics such as reading time and fixation count. → Field colors Give a field a highlight color. Its ✕ puts it back to the default gray. → Refresh fields Check again which fields have one value per trial. Screen and its ◀ ▶ On a trial recorded over several screens: the screen to show.

docs.title: Plot controls
docs.text: The column on the right of the plot. At the top, the modes and designs change the whole figure at once. Under them, each layer of the figure has a row: the switch turns the layer on or off, and the ▾ beside it opens that layer's settings, described below one menu at a time. The last two rows, Filters & highlights and Figure & canvas, cover the figure as a whole. A grayed-out control says why when you hover over it. Essentials shows only the view tiles and Palette; the rest of this section is in Full.

docs.title: Animate: play the reading as a video
docs.text:
The Animate switch turns the figure into an animation, a video of the reading played back fixation by fixation, with play and pause buttons and a time slider above the plot. While it is on, the Fixations, Heatmap and Raw gaze switches are grayed. Its ▾ holds:

Control What it does Replay → Speed How fast the video plays, from ×0.25 to ×8: ×1 is the participant's recorded pace, ×2 twice as fast, ×0.5 half as fast. Replay → Autoplay → On load Start playing the animation as soon as the plot is shown. Otherwise it starts when you click play. Replay → Duration For information only: the trial's reading time, and how long the video runs at this speed. Frames → Quality How smooth the video is: Coarse, Standard or Fine. More frames play more smoothly but take longer to build. Moving either slider below makes it Custom. Frames → Every Reading time between frames, in ms. Frames → Limit The most frames a video gets. A long trial gets wider frame steps to fit. Frames → Result For information only: how many frames this trial's video has, and how far apart they ended up.

docs.title: Compare
docs.text:
The Compare switch shows a second scanpath, B, beside or over this one. Pick B in the trial control bar, above the plot. Its ▾ holds:

Control What it does View Overlay both scanpaths, or give each a panel, Side by side or Top & bottom. With Animate on, the comparison is an overlay. Stimulus from In an overlay, whose word boxes and text are drawn: Both, A or B. Label A / Label B Each scanpath's name in the Compare (A/B) legend, written with fields such as {participant_id}. Empty uses the automatic label. Shown while that legend is on. Available fields The fields a label can use. Step → A and B together ◀ ▶ move both scanpaths at once.

docs.title: Design presets and palette
docs.text:
Restyle the whole figure in one click, with a ready-made design or one you saved:

Control What it does Scanpath / Heatmap / Illustration Ready-made designs: fixations and saccades over the text, a word-box heatmap, or a clean schematic. Custom Your most recent hand-made settings. My designs Your saved designs. Click one to apply it. renames it and deletes it. My designs → Save the settings on screen as a named design, to apply again later in one click. My designs → Export / Import Download your designs as a file, or load a file of designs, to share a look with co-authors or move your designs to another computer. A design in the file replaces yours of the same name. Palette A color scheme for the whole figure: Default (colorblind-safe), Print / grayscale or High contrast. It reads Custom once you change one of its colors.

docs.title: Fixations
docs.text:
The Fixations switch draws the fixation markers. Its ▾ holds:

Control What it does Marker → Color What decides each marker's color. One color, the default, paints them all alike. Pick a number column of the fixations, such as duration or time, and the markers follow a color scale: with the default blues, longer fixations show darker. Pick a category, such as Text line or a part-of-speech column, and each value gets a color, with a legend. Marker → color box With One color: the fixation marker color. With a number column: the color scale. Marker → Range When markers are colored by a number: the values at the two ends of the color scale. Auto fits each trial. Marker → Shape Choose the fixation marker shape: circle, square, diamond, triangle, cross, X, star, hexagon or heart. Marker → Size Set the marker size range: the smallest and largest marker diameter, in px. Marker → Scale Choose how duration sets marker size: square root (the default), linear, log, or relative to this figure (its shortest to its longest fixation). Marker → Durations Set the durations (ms) that get the smallest and the largest marker. Not used on the relative scale. Marker → Opacity Set the fixation marker opacity. Lower it to see overlapping fixations. Marker → Outline Set the width (px) and color of the ring around each marker. A width of 0 draws none. Color bar → Show Show the color scale's bar, when markers are colored by a number. Color bar → Vertical / Horizontal, Angle, Size, Thickness, Length Set the bar's direction (right of the plot or below it), its tick-label angle and size, and its thickness and length. Fixation index → Show Number each fixation in reading order. Fixation index → color, Size Choose the numbers' color and size. Snap → To line Move each fixation up or down onto its line of text. This makes a schematic, labeled Illustration. Snap → Position Choose where on its line a snapped fixation sits.

docs.title: Saccades
docs.text:
The Saccades switch draws the lines between fixations. Its ▾ holds:

Control What it does Line → Color Choose what decides the saccade color: One color for all; Forward / regression, two colors; or By type, a color per saccade type (forward, skip, refixation, return sweep, regression), with a legend. Forward / regression and By type need a word ID for each fixation, the word it landed on, mapped as the Fixations table's Word ID (such as EyeLink's CURRENT_FIX_INTEREST_AREA_ID). Without one, every saccade is drawn as Off the text. Line → color box With One color: the saccade line color. Line → Types With Forward / regression or By type: the color of each group, such as regressions or return sweeps. Line → Style Choose the saccade line style: solid, dashed, dotted or dash-dot. Line → Width Set the saccade line width (thickness), in px. Line → Opacity Set the saccade line and arrow opacity. Lower it to bring the fixations forward. Shape Choose the saccade shape. Straight draws lines. Arc draws arcs over the text, a schematic labeled Illustration. Direction arrows → Show Show saccade direction arrows: an arrowhead on each saccade, pointing where the eye went. Direction arrows → Arrow size Set the saccade arrowhead size.

docs.title: Stimulus
docs.text:
The Stimulus switch draws the text and the stimulus image. The text rows start from the dataset's Recording setup, and changes here apply to the figure only. Its ▾ holds:

Control What it does Text → Show Show the stimulus text, the words the participant read, at their place on the screen. Text → Redact Draw a rounded block over each word's letters instead of the word, in the text color, and hide the word in the hovers, so a figure shows where the text was without showing what it said. Fit → Fit to word boxes Size the stimulus text from its word boxes, instead of a fixed font size. Fit → Spacing With Fit to word boxes on: the distance between lines, in font sizes. The font size is that distance divided by this value, so 3 leaves a blank line above and below. Size With Fit to word boxes on: the size of the axis and legend text, in px. Off: the stimulus text's size too, in px or pt. Font Choose the stimulus text font (typeface). Other font… takes any font name. Color → text color Choose the stimulus text color. Color → Background Choose the plot background color: a preset, or any color in the box beside it. Highlight words → Show Highlight words in the stimulus text, such as the answer span. Highlight words → word column Choose which words to highlight: a true/false word column, such as the critical span. Style Choose the word highlight style, Mark text (colored text) or Mark border (a border around the words), and the highlight color. Image → Show Show the stimulus image, the screen as shown in the experiment, under the scanpath. File Upload a stimulus image (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP) to draw under the scanpath. It replaces the dataset's image and is not included in Share links. Opacity Set the stimulus image opacity. Lower it so the scanpath reads over it. Offset → X / Y Move (nudge) the stimulus image left, right, up or down, in px, to line it up with the word boxes. Scale Resize (scale) the stimulus image so its text matches the word boxes.

docs.title: Word boxes
docs.text:
The Word boxes switch draws each word's box (its interest area). Its ▾ holds:

Control What it does Box → Line color Choose the word box outline (border) color. Box → Line opacity Set the word box outline opacity. 0 hides the outlines. Box → Fill color Choose the word box fill color, inside each box. Box → Fill opacity Set the word box fill opacity. 0 draws outlines only.

docs.title: Heatmap
docs.text:
The Heatmap switch shows where reading concentrated. Its ▾ holds:

Control What it does Style Choose the heatmap style: Word boxes colors each word box, Smoothed blurs the fixations with a Gaussian. Compare always uses word boxes. Blur For Smoothed: how far each fixation spreads, in px. Auto picks it from the size of the data. Color → By Choose what the heatmap measures: total fixation duration (dwell time), or Fixation count. Color → Colors Choose the heatmap colors (color scale). Scale Choose a linear or log heatmap scale. Range For word-box heatmaps, fix the color range across trials. Auto runs from 0 to the trial's highest value. Smoothed heatmaps are scaled to each figure's peak. Opacity Set the heatmap opacity. Auto uses 0.5 for word boxes and 0.45 for smoothed. Color bar → Show, orientation, Angle, Size, Thickness, Length Show the heatmap color bar, and set its orientation, label angle and size, thickness and length.

docs.title: Raw gaze
docs.text:
The Raw gaze switch draws the gaze samples as recorded. Its ▾ holds:

Control What it does Marker → Color Not used outside Compare: the samples are colored by their time, or by their order when they have no timestamps. Marker → Size Set the raw gaze sample marker size. Marker → Opacity Set the raw gaze sample opacity.

docs.title: Filters & highlights
docs.text:
Which fixations and saccades are drawn, and which stand out:

Control What it does Fixations → Index range Show only some fixations: a range of the reading order, such as fixations 10 to 40. Fixations → All trials Keep that fixation range when you move to another trial. Off, it applies to this trial only, and the next trial shows all its fixations. Short / Long Find fixations shorter or longer than a duration threshold (80 ms and 800 ms by default). Each row's Mode is Off, Highlight or Hide. Highlight marks the fixations. Hide hides their markers, but saccades and the heatmap still use them. Outside the text Highlight or hide fixations that land in no word box. Near a blink Highlight or hide fixations at or next to a blink (needs a blink column). Marker and Color Choose the marker shape and color of each highlighted fixation kind. Saccades → Types Show only some saccade types, such as regressions or return sweeps. Empty draws all. Needs a word ID for each fixation, as for coloring saccades by type.

docs.title: Figure & canvas
docs.text:
The figure as a whole:

Control What it does Frame → Crop to data Crop (zoom) the figure to the part of the screen with data, instead of the whole screen. Margin Set the crop margin: the space around the data when cropping. Auto uses 5% of the data's width and height, at least 20 px. Border → Show, color Show a 1 px border around the plot area, and choose its color. It marks the edge of the screen, or, with Crop to data, the edge of the cropped area. Grid → Show Show a grid of screen coordinates, in px. Grid → Auto, interval Set the grid spacing (interval), in px, or let Auto choose it. Labels Set the grid label (tick label) font size. Axes → X / Y Choose the x and y axis fields. X / Y draws the reading on the screen. Any other pair turns the figure into a scatter plot (chart) of the fixations, with no text, word boxes, saccades, heatmap or grid. Animate and Compare always plot X / Y. For example: Time (ms) against X for a time course of the reading, where regressions show as dips; Time (ms) against Word # for reading progress through the text; Fixation # against Duration (ms) for fixation durations over the trial. Illustration → Label Choose when the figure carries an Illustration note, saying it does not show the recorded positions. Auto adds it when a setting changes the geometry or the data (such as snapping fixations to a line or drawing saccades as arcs), Show always, Hide never. Illustration → Text Write the Illustration label's text. Empty writes "Illustration ·" followed by the reasons. Title → Show, text, Size Add a figure title above the plot, and set its font size. {field} inserts a value of the trial. Caption → Show, text, Size, color Add a figure caption below the plot, and set its font size and color. {field} works here too. Credit → Show Add a small Made with Scanpath Studio line under the plot. Hover → Words / Fixations Choose the hover fields: what the tooltip shows when the mouse is over a word or a fixation. Legends → Show Show or hide each legend the figure draws: Compare (A/B), Saccade types, Fixation colors, Fixation sizes or Text highlight. Each has a row. Legends → Position Choose the legend position: a corner, the middle of an edge, or down a side, outside or inside the plot. Legends → Arrangement Choose the legend arrangement: Stacked or Side by side. Legends → Text size Set the legend text (font) size, in px. Empty uses the figure's text size.

docs.title: Reset visualization
docs.text:
The button at the foot of the column.

Control What it does Reset visualization After you confirm, reset every plot setting to its default, Filters & highlights included. Annotations, trial filters, data and the selected trial stay.

docs.title: In Compare
docs.text:
With Compare on, scanpath B gets a second row in the trial control bar, and several menus split into a Scanpath A and a Scanpath B group.

Control What it does Dataset B Choose the dataset scanpath B comes from: this one, or another dataset. Trial B, slider, ◀ ▶ Choose scanpath B's trial: 📄 marks the same text, 👤 the same participant. Screen B On a trial recorded over several screens: B's screen to show. ⇅ on B's row Sort scanpath B's trial list, apart from A's. The default, Same text, then same participant, lists trials of A's text first, then A's participant, then the rest. You can also sort by any field, as on A's row. on B's row Filter scanpath B's trials, apart from A's. Fixations ▾ → Scanpath A / B → Color, Size, Opacity Choose each scanpath's fixation marker color, size range and opacity. When the markers are colored by a column, Color becomes Outline. Saccades ▾ → Scanpath A / B → Color, Style, Width Choose each scanpath's saccade line color, style and width. Word boxes ▾ → Scanpath A / B → Line, Fill Choose each scanpath's word box outline and fill colors and opacities. Heatmap ▾ → Scanpath A / B → Colors Choose each scanpath's heatmap colors (color scale). Raw gaze ▾ → Scanpath A / B → Color Choose each scanpath's raw gaze sample color. Filters & highlights ▾ → Fixations · B / Saccades · B Set scanpath B's fixation range, fixation highlights and saccade types.

docs.title: Under the plot
docs.text:
The tabs under the figure. Essentials has Export, for the current figure, and Share; the other tabs and the export bundle are in Full.

Tab Control What it does Annotations Favorite Star the trial as a favorite, to find it again with Favorites only in the trial filters. Tags / Add a tag Tag the trial, with an existing tag or a new one, such as exclude. Tags let you filter the trial list later: the in the trial control bar keeps or hides trials by tag. Notes Write a free-text note on the trial. Stimulus & context Fields → Context fields Choose the trial context to show, such as the text's title, a question or an answer. Fields → Highlighted spans Choose true/false word columns to highlight in the text, each with a summary line. Comparisons Match field Compare with other trials: show the trials that share this trial's value of a field, such as the same text. Columns Set how many comparison panels per row, from 1 to 4. Export Download format Export (download) the figure on screen as PNG, SVG, PDF or HTML, or the animation as an HTML, GIF or MP4 video. Width, unit, DPI Set the PNG export size for print: width (mm or in) and resolution (DPI). A blank width writes the figure at three times its screen size. Trials to include Choose which trials to export in the bundle: This trial, All filtered trials, All trials of one participant, All trials of one text, or All trials, ignoring filters. Formats / Tabular data / Table format Choose the bundle's figure formats, the data tables to include, and their format (CSV, Parquet or both). Layers as separate files Export each visual layer (fixations, saccades, word boxes…) as a separate file, to stack in a vector editor. Annotations (JSON) / Settings file (JSON) Settings file: beside each trial's figure, a plot_config.json recording how it was drawn (layers, colors, sizes, screen, title and caption), so the figures are documented. Annotations: one annotations.json with the exported trials' favorites, tags and notes, which Data Management → Annotations can import again. File path pattern Set the file names inside the export bundle. Build export Build the export bundle (a zip) to download. Share Link Copy a share link that reopens this trial with these settings. The data doesn't travel in the link, so whoever opens it needs the same dataset. The bundled demo works anywhere. A public dataset has to be downloaded on their side. For your own dataset, send its files and setup file ( Edit dataset → Download setup file) so they can add it first. A link made on your own computer (a localhost address) opens only where the app runs at that same address. Code → Python / CLI, Show every option Get the Python or command-line code that redraws this figure, for scripts and reproduction. Settings file → Download settings / Restore settings Save the plot settings to a file, or load (restore) a saved settings file.

  • Analyze a corpus

In the app, open Help → Tutorials for guided tours of the controls. They use the Full mode, and starting one switches that visit to it.

docs.title: Analyze a corpus
docs.text:
• Analyze one text

    Compare word-by-word measures across participants.

  • Compare groups or conditions

    Inspect group means and differences.

  • See progression over time

    Inspect trends within or across trials.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: Open a dataset and set the trial filters for your question. Word-level views need reading measures in the Words table; the bundled demo includes them. To compare participants on one text, their trials of that text must share one text ID.

docs.title: Keep the result
docs.text:
⬇ Download this table (CSV) saves the values. ⬇ Download the recipe (JSON) saves the dataset name, the trial filters, the analysis choices and the counts. The recipe names the dataset but holds none of its data, so keep the source data to reproduce the result.

To draw a summary with Python or the CLI, see Plot a summary in code.

docs.title: Analyze one text
docs.text:
Compare how participants read the words of one text.

  1. Select the trials, then open Corpus Analysis → Per text.
  2. Pick a text and a reading measure your data provides.
  3. In View, choose Measure on the stimulus. To plot the measure against a word feature such as surprisal, choose Measure vs feature and pick the Feature. Your Words table must have that column.
  4. In Aggregate, choose how the values are combined. Cohort profile also draws a Spread band, and its Min participants per word leaves out words that too few participants have a value for.
  5. Download the table and recipe.

The recording shows total fixation duration on a text, against GPT-2 surprisal, and between two groups.

docs.title: Compare groups or conditions
docs.text:
Compare a reading measure between two groups of participants or two conditions.

  1. Select the trials, then open Corpus Analysis → Groups.
  2. Turn on Compare a second group.
  3. Choose Split a field to form the groups from the values of one column, or Independent filter sets to define each group by a separate set of filters.
  4. In View, choose Group means & difference and a measure. Check the number of participants in each group and whether any participant is in both. The Standardized difference (Cohen's d) is shown only when the groups share no participant.
  5. Download the table and recipe.

The comparison is descriptive. It runs no significance test. For a recorded example, see Analyze one text.

docs.title: See progression over time
docs.text:
Inspect a measure within trials or across a session.

  1. Select the trials and open Corpus Analysis.

  2. Choose the view for the question:

    Scope View One participant across trials Per participant → Per-trial trend Fixation duration within trials, pooled for one participant Per participant → Fixation duration over time A group across trials Groups → Group trend

  3. Choose a measure, and an Aggregate where the view offers one. Across-trial trends order each participant's trials by a trial_index or TRIAL_INDEX column. Without one, the app orders them by fixation time, or as listed, and this may differ from the order the trials were shown. For the within-trial view, set X axis to Fixation order, or to Time (ms) when the data records fixation onsets.

  4. Download the table and recipe.

docs.title: Optimize data collection
docs.text:
• Check a session

    Inspect a pilot or completed recording.

  • Compare two eye trackers

    Review recordings of the same text.

  • Audit an experimenter

    Review sessions by who collected them.

Start with a loaded dataset. To apply exclusion decisions after reviewing, use Filter data.

docs.title: Audit an experimenter
docs.text:
Review recordings collected by one experimenter.

These steps use the Full mode: switch to it in the top bar of the Scanpath view, or add ui=full to the app's address (Essentials and Full).

  1. Keep the experimenter column when you import the data, under Extra fields to keep. If each participant had one experimenter, you can instead attach it in a participant metadata table.
  2. Open the filter () beside Select trial and choose the experimenter. Columns of a participant metadata table are under By participant.
  3. Inspect and replay their trials.
  4. In Annotations, tag trials review and note recurring problems.
  5. Export the review.

To compare experimenters, turn on Compare. Use the filter on each scanpath's row to pick a different experimenter, and choose readings of the same text.

docs.title: Check a session
docs.text:
Inspect a recording and save the trials that need attention.

These steps use the Full mode: switch to it in the top bar of the Scanpath view, or add ui=full to the app's address (Essentials and Full).

docs.title: 1. Open the session
docs.text: Import your tables, or select a loaded dataset. Check that its Recording setup matches the screen used in the experiment.

docs.title: 2. Inspect a trial
docs.text:
In the Scanpath view, pick a trial in Select trial. Turn on Word boxes and check:

  • whether the boxes match the stimulus image, if you have one;
  • where the fixations sit relative to the words;
  • unexpected gaps, shifts or off-screen positions.

For a consistent offset, check coordinate units and screen setup.

docs.title: 3. Replay the recording
docs.text: Turn on Animate to follow the fixation order and timing. To mark short or long fixations, or fixations outside the text, open Filters & highlights ▾ → Fixations and set Short, Long or Outside the text to Highlight. A gap or an unusual scanpath does not tell you its cause.

docs.title: 4. Record the review
docs.text: In Annotations, tag the trial review and write what you observed in Notes. Use ◀ ▶ beside Select trial to move through the session.

docs.title: 5. Save the review
docs.text:
Export favorites, tags and notes from Data Management → Annotations → Export. The file includes participant and trial IDs. Open on an annotation row returns to that trial.

For exclusion decisions, follow Exclude unsuitable trials.

docs.title: Compare two eye trackers
docs.text:
Review the same text recorded with two trackers or setups.

These steps use the Full mode: switch to it in the top bar of the Scanpath view, or add ui=full to the app's address (Essentials and Full).

  1. Import each recording as a separate dataset, each with the Recording setup of its tracker.
  2. Open the first dataset in the Scanpath view and pick a trial.
  3. Turn on Compare. In scanpath B's row, choose the second dataset in Dataset B and a trial of the same text in Trial B.
  4. Compare fixation placement, spread and missing stretches. An overlay needs both datasets recorded on the same screen size. Otherwise the app shows the two scanpaths side by side.

This recording compares two participants in the bundled demo. For two trackers, choose the second recording in Dataset B.

Use the session-review steps to save observations.

docs.title: Filter data
docs.text:
• Exclude unsuitable trials

    Leave tagged trials out.

  • Select participants by a field

    Use participant metadata.

  • Find the trials an analysis needs

    Select trials after inspecting fixations.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: Open a dataset in the Scanpath view. The filter () beside Select trial selects whole trials. Filters & highlights in the Plot controls changes which fixations and saccades the figure draws. Both, and the export these tasks end with, are in the Full mode: switch to it in the top bar of the Scanpath view, or add ui=full to the app's address (Essentials and Full).

docs.title: Check and export the selection
docs.text:
1. Check the remaining trial and participant counts and inspect a few trials.
  2. Follow Export every trial and choose All filtered trials. The bundle's index.csv lists its files with their participant and trial IDs.
  3. Keep a full decision record with Data Management → Annotations → Export. The annotations in a bundle cover only the exported trials.

docs.title: Exclude unsuitable trials
docs.text:
Apply your exclusion criteria and leave rejected trials out of the selection.

These steps use the Full mode: switch to it in the top bar of the Scanpath view, or add ui=full to the app's address (Essentials and Full).

  1. Review the session. Judge each trial against your study's criteria. A scanpath pattern alone does not establish skimming or poor calibration.
  2. In Annotations, tag rejected trials exclude and write a short reason in Notes.
  3. Open the filter () beside Select trial. Under By trial annotation, add exclude to Excluding tags.
  4. Check and export the selection.

For a trial with several screens, tag the whole trial. A tag on one screen does not exclude the trial.

The recording shows favorites and tags. For the selection above, use the exclude tag and Excluding tags.

docs.title: Find the trials an analysis needs
docs.text:
Locate trials containing particular fixation patterns.

These steps use the Full mode: switch to it in the top bar of the Scanpath view, or add ui=full to the app's address (Essentials and Full).

  1. Open Filters & highlights ▾ → Fixations.

  2. Set the Mode of the category you need to Highlight:

    • Short or Long, with a duration threshold in ms
    • Outside the text, for fixations in no word box
    • Near a blink, if your data has a blink column

  3. Step through the trials. In Annotations, tag those that meet your analysis criteria, for example include.

  4. Open the filter () beside Select trial. Under By trial annotation, add include to With any of these tags.
  5. Check and export the selection.

docs.title: Select participants by a field
docs.text:
Select participants using metadata such as native language, age or group.

These steps use the Full mode: switch to it in the top bar of the Scanpath view, or add ui=full to the app's address (Essentials and Full).

  1. Attach a participant metadata table, with one row per participant and a participant ID column. When you add a dataset, use Metadata → Participants. For a loaded dataset, use Data Management → Edit dataset → Data tables & column mapping.
  2. Open the filter () beside Select trial and find By participant.
  3. Choose a field and the values or range to keep.
  4. Check the remaining participant IDs and export the selection.

To also apply trial-level quality criteria, follow Exclude unsuitable trials.

docs.title: Export customized figures
docs.text:
• Export one figure

    A static image or interactive HTML.

  • Export a replay

    GIF, MP4 or interactive HTML.

  • Export every trial

    A ZIP of figures and data tables.

For installation requirements or a failed export, see the export FAQ.

docs.title: Export a replay
docs.text:
Save an animated reading for a talk or supplement.

These steps use the Full mode: switch to it in the top bar of the Scanpath view, or add ui=full to the app's address (Essentials and Full).

  1. Pick a trial in the Scanpath view and turn on Animate.
  2. In Animate ▾ → Replay, set the Speed. Turn on the layers you want to show.
  3. Open the Export tab. Under Current figure, set Download format to GIF, MP4 or HTML.
  4. Download the replay. GIF and MP4 play at the selected speed. HTML keeps the interactive playback controls.

Exporting a GIF. The recording shortens the rendering wait.

For GIF/MP4 export from Python, see Export and share.

docs.title: Export every trial
docs.text:
Build a ZIP of static figures and data tables for a set of trials.

These steps use the Full mode: switch to it in the top bar of the Scanpath view, or add ui=full to the app's address (Essentials and Full).

  1. Set the figure's design once. Each exported trial uses that design, without animation or a comparison partner.
  2. Open the Export tab. Under Export bundle → Trials to include, choose This trial, All filtered trials, All trials of one participant, All trials of one text or All trials, ignoring filters.
  3. Choose the Figure formats and, under Also include, the tables and their Table format. Check the File path pattern. To edit individual layers later, turn on Layers as separate files.
  4. Click Build export, download the bundle, and inspect one exported figure.

Exporting figures and tables for the bundled demo's trials. The recording speeds up the build.

Keep each trial's plot_config.json for the design, README.md for the build details and index.csv for the file list and failures. Keep your original data and record its version and the selected trial filters separately.

For a scripted batch, use the Python recipe in Export and share.

docs.title: Export one figure
docs.text:
Save a scanpath, heatmap or comparison at the size you need.

Design presets, Compare and My designs are in the Full mode: switch to it in the top bar of the Scanpath view, or add ui=full to the app's address (Essentials and Full). In Essentials, the view tiles choose the figure.

docs.title: 1. Choose the view
docs.text: Pick a trial in the Scanpath view. Choose one of the Design presets, or set the layers in the Plot controls. Turn on Compare if the figure needs two readings. Check that text and markers are readable and nothing is clipped.

docs.title: 2. Set the format and size
docs.text:
Open the Export tab and find Current figure. Choose the Download format:

Output Format Image PNG Vector figure SVG or PDF Interactive figure HTML

For a print PNG, set Width and DPI. For HTML that opens offline, tick Self-contained HTML.

docs.title: 3. Download
docs.text:
Click the download button for the chosen format, such as ⬇ Download PNG.

Exporting a PNG at 180 mm and 300 dpi.

docs.title: 4. Reuse the design or share the figure
docs.text:
• My designs in the Plot controls saves the look for other trials.
  • Share → Link reopens the trial and its settings. The link does not carry data you uploaded, so load that data separately.
  • Share → Code gives Python or CLI code that redraws the figure.
  • Share → Settings file → Download settings saves the settings, and Restore settings loads them again.
